aidDo: Help the person sit down and rest in a comfortable half-sitting position. Loosen tight clothing. Keep them calm and still.
aidDont: Do not let them walk around or exert themselves. Do not leave them alone.
escalate: If pain lasts more than a few minutes, spreads to arm/jaw, or breathing becomes difficult.

aidDo: Sit the person upright, not lying down. Ensure fresh air/ventilation. Loosen tight clothing around neck and chest.
aidDont: Do not force them to lie flat. Do not give food or water.
escalate: If lips/fingertips turn bluish or they cannot speak full sentences.

aidDo: Keep upright, loosen clothing, check airway for visible blockage.
aidDont: Do not attempt to give water. Do not leave unattended.
escalate: Immediately — this is always an ambulance situation.

aidDo: Apply firm, direct pressure on the wound with a clean cloth. Elevate the injured area above heart level if possible.
aidDont: Do not remove an embedded object. Do not repeatedly lift the cloth to check.
escalate: If bleeding does not slow within 10 minutes of firm pressure or the person becomes faint.

aidDo: Keep the person still, don't move them unless there is immediate danger (fire, traffic). Keep them warm and calm.
aidDont: Do not move the neck/spine. Do not remove a helmet forcefully.
escalate: Always — call ambulance immediately for any accident with visible injury.

aidDo: Immobilize the limb using a splint or firm support (rolled newspaper, board). Support the joints above and below the injury.
aidDont: Do not try to straighten or realign the bone. Do not let the person bear weight on it.
escalate: If bone is visibly exposed, or the limb is cold/pale/numb below the injury.

aidDo: Keep the person still and calm. Apply a clean cloth with gentle pressure if there's a scalp wound. Watch for changes in alertness.
aidDont: Do not let them fall asleep if disoriented. Do not give food or water.
escalate: If there is vomiting, confusion, unequal pupils, or loss of consciousness.

aidDo: Lay the person on their side (recovery position) if breathing normally. Check the airway is clear. Loosen tight clothing.
aidDont: Do not give anything by mouth. Do not leave them lying on their back.
escalate: Immediately — always call ambulance.

aidDo: Note the exact time symptoms started (critical for stroke treatment). Keep the person calm and seated or lying safely.
aidDont: Do not give food, water, or medication.
escalate: Immediately — treat as suspected stroke, time-critical.

aidDo: Note the exact time symptoms started. Keep the person still and reassured.
aidDont: Do not give food or water — swallowing may be impaired.
escalate: Immediately — treat as suspected stroke.

aidDo: Note the time it started. Help the person into a safe, comfortable position, avoiding falls.
aidDont: Do not force the affected limb to move. Do not give food or water.
escalate: Immediately — treat as suspected stroke.

aidDo: Clear the area of hard/sharp objects. Cushion the head. Turn them onto their side once the seizure stops.
aidDont: Do not restrain their movements. Do not put anything in their mouth. Do not give water until fully alert.
escalate: If the seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, or another follows immediately.

aidDo: Help the person lie down in a comfortable position, often with knees bent. Keep them still.
aidDont: Do not give food, water, or pain medication. Do not apply heat to the abdomen.
escalate: If pain is sudden and severe, with fever, vomiting, or a rigid abdomen.

aidDo: Keep the person sitting up or on their side to prevent choking. Keep calm and still.
aidDont: Do not give food or water.
escalate: Immediately — always an emergency.

aidDo: Cool the burn under cool (not ice-cold) running water for 10–20 minutes. Remove nearby jewellery/tight clothing before swelling starts.
aidDont: Do not apply ice, butter, oil, or toothpaste. Do not burst any blisters.
escalate: If the burn is larger than the palm, on the face/hands/genitals, or the skin is charred/white.

aidDo: Keep the person calm and still to slow venom spread. Keep the bitten limb below heart level. Remove tight clothing/jewellery near the bite.
aidDont: Do not cut, suck, or apply ice to the bite. Do not apply a tight tourniquet.
escalate: Immediately — always requires hospital care and anti-venom.

aidDo: Try to identify what was consumed and keep the container/packaging for the hospital. Keep the person calm.
aidDont: Do not induce vomiting unless specifically instructed. Do not give milk or water unless advised.
escalate: Immediately — call ambulance/poison helpline.

aidDo: Keep the person on their side if drowsy, to protect their airway. Stay with them and monitor breathing.
aidDont: Do not leave them alone. Do not try to make them vomit.
escalate: Immediately — always an emergency.

aidDo: Keep the person cool and hydrated with sips of water. Use a lukewarm sponge if fever is very high.
aidDont: Do not use ice-cold water or wrap in blankets. Do not give aspirin to children.
escalate: If fever exceeds 104°F/40°C, or the rash spreads with a stiff neck or confusion.

aidDo: Keep the person calm, time the contractions, and arrange transport to a maternity-equipped hospital.
aidDont: Do not delay travel once contractions are close together. Do not give food.
escalate: If there is bleeding, severe pain, or reduced baby movement.

aidDo: Have the person lie down and rest, ideally on their left side. Keep calm.
aidDont: Do not insert anything internally. Do not delay seeking care.
escalate: Immediately — always an emergency in pregnancy.

aidDo: Keep the child in light clothing, offer fluids, use a lukewarm sponge if very hot.
aidDont: Do not use ice-cold water or over-bundle the child. Do not give adult-dose medication.
escalate: If fever is above 104°F/40°C, or the child has a seizure, rash, or is unusually drowsy.

aidDo: Keep the baby warm and in a safe, flat position. Check nothing is blocking the nose/mouth.
aidDont: Do not shake the baby. Do not delay — newborns deteriorate fast.
escalate: Immediately — always an emergency.

aidDo: Rinse gently with clean water if a chemical is involved. Cover the eye loosely with a clean cloth.
aidDont: Do not rub the eye. Do not try to remove an embedded object.
escalate: Always seek immediate care for eye injuries.

aidDo: Keep the person seated and calm. Avoid strain on the eyes.
aidDont: Do not rub the eyes. Do not delay care.
escalate: Immediately — sudden vision loss is always urgent.

aidDo: Let fluid drain naturally; place a clean cloth loosely over the outer ear.
aidDont: Do not plug the ear canal. Do not insert anything into the ear.
escalate: If bleeding follows a head injury, or is accompanied by hearing loss/dizziness.

aidDo: If choking and the person can cough, encourage coughing. If they cannot breathe/speak, give back blows and abdominal thrusts if trained.
aidDont: Do not perform blind finger sweeps in the mouth.
escalate: Immediately if the person cannot breathe, speak, or is turning blue.

aidDo: Rinse mouth with warm water. A cold compress on the cheek can ease swelling.
aidDont: Do not apply aspirin directly to the gum or tooth.
escalate: If there is facial swelling, fever, or difficulty swallowing/breathing.

aidDo: Stay with the person, listen without judgment, remove access to means of harm if safe to do so.
aidDont: Do not leave them alone. Do not argue or dismiss their feelings.
escalate: Immediately — contact emergency services or a crisis helpline.

aidDo: Encourage slow, steady breathing. Speak calmly and reassure them they are safe.
aidDont: Do not dismiss the episode or tell them to 'calm down' abruptly.
escalate: If chest pain, breathlessness, or symptoms don't ease — rule out cardiac causes.

aidDo: Help the person find a comfortable position; a warm compress on the back/side may ease pain.
aidDont: Do not give large amounts of fluid without medical advice if vomiting.
escalate: If fever, inability to urinate, or blood in urine appears.

aidDo: Keep the person calm and comfortable while arranging transport.
aidDont: Do not apply pressure to the lower abdomen.
escalate: If painful, or accompanied by fever or abdominal swelling.

aidDo: Remove the suspected trigger if known. Apply a cool compress to itchy areas.
aidDont: Do not scratch. Do not apply unknown creams.
escalate: If swelling of face/lips/tongue or breathing difficulty develops.

aidDo: Help the person use their epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen) if they have one. Keep them lying down with legs raised unless breathing is difficult.
aidDont: Do not let them stand or walk. Do not wait to see if it improves on its own.
escalate: Immediately — always call ambulance even if symptoms seem to improve.

aidDo: Begin CPR immediately if trained (chest compressions), and use an AED if available.
aidDont: Do not stop compressions except to use a defibrillator or when help arrives.
escalate: Immediately — call ambulance while starting CPR.

aidDo: If conscious, give a fast-acting sugar source (juice, sugar water, glucose tablet).
aidDont: Do not give food/drink if the person is drowsy or unconscious — choking risk.
escalate: If they don't improve within 10–15 minutes or lose consciousness.

aidDo: Keep the person calm and hydrated with water if conscious.
aidDont: Do not give sugary food/drinks.
escalate: If breath smells fruity, breathing is rapid, or confusion sets in.

aidDo: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water for several minutes. Cover with a clean bandage.
aidDont: Do not apply home remedies like chili powder or oil to the wound.
escalate: Always seek medical care for rabies risk assessment, even for minor bites.

aidDo: Turn off the power source before touching the person, or use a non-conductive object to separate them from the source.
aidDont: Do not touch the person directly while they are still in contact with the electrical source.
escalate: Immediately — always an emergency, even if the person seems fine afterward.

aidDo: Once safely out of water, check breathing and begin CPR if needed. Keep the person warm.
aidDont: Do not assume they are fine just because they're conscious — delayed complications can occur.
escalate: Immediately — always seek medical evaluation after any near-drowning.

aidDo: Help the person sit upright and use their reliever inhaler if they have one. Keep them calm.
aidDont: Do not have them lie down. Do not let them exert themselves.
escalate: If the inhaler doesn't help within a few minutes, or lips turn blue.

aidDo: Move to a cool/shaded place, remove excess clothing, cool the skin with water or damp cloths, fan them.
aidDont: Do not give fluids if they are confused or unconscious.
escalate: If body temperature is very high, confusion sets in, or they stop sweating.

aidDo: Encourage rest in a comfortable position. Apply a cold pack for the first 24–48 hours if from injury.
aidDont: Do not force movement or lift heavy objects.
escalate: If there is numbness, weakness in the legs, or loss of bladder/bowel control.

aidDo: Rest the joint, apply a cold compress, and elevate if possible.
aidDont: Do not continue using the joint under load.
escalate: If the joint is deformed, very hot to touch, or fever is present.

aidDo: No immediate first aid needed; note size, location, and how long it has been present.
aidDont: Do not attempt to squeeze or drain the lump.
escalate: Seek prompt (non-emergency) evaluation, especially if rapidly growing.

aidDo: No immediate first aid needed; keep a record of diet, symptoms, and duration.
aidDont: Do not self-medicate based on assumptions.
escalate: Seek prompt evaluation, especially if accompanied by fatigue or pain.

aidDo: Keep the person hydrated and rested.
aidDont: Do not give alcohol or unnecessary medication, which can stress the liver further.
escalate: If accompanied by confusion, severe abdominal pain, or dark urine.

aidDo: Keep the person calm and monitor fluid intake as advised.
aidDont: Do not force large amounts of fluid without medical guidance.
escalate: If accompanied by swelling, breathlessness, or confusion.

aidDo: Keep the person completely still, support the head and neck in the position found.
aidDont: Do not move or twist the neck/back under any circumstances. Do not let them sit up.
escalate: Always — treat any suspected spinal injury as an emergency.

aidDo: No first aid required; this is a non-urgent consultation matter.
aidDont: N/A
escalate: Not applicable — book a routine consultation.
